rows.what_the_ink_shows: The subscript after the first right-hand S is Y: its two curved upper arms meet above a long diagonal descending tail with a hooked end; see crops/14_scan026_L255_SY.jpg. The adjacent T and T-prime subscripts have conspicuous horizontal top bars and short upright stems, unlike this Y; see crops/14_scan026_L255_comparison.jpg. The visible expression is S_Y(nu)=0.
rows.note: Written: S_Y(nu)=0. Intended, as identified by the supplied correction and compatible with the page’s statement that nu is a zero-cycle of T: S_T(nu)=0, using the Albanese map of the parameter variety T. Treat Y as the author’s retained earlier notation and do not normalize it to T. The original LaTeX is S_{\unsure{Y|T}}(\nu); under the rule that decision (b) has no page edit, the candidate retains that inherited wrapper, although this visual review finds the ink reading Y secure. Main reader is explicitly notified of this source-wrapper issue.
